before_question.question: After being played once, do Anti-Matter Super, Cudgel Super, Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super, or Machine Wild automatically apply in later encounters, or must the corresponding flare be played again each encounter its effect is desired?

required_facts: Each listed flare must be played in each encounter in which its effect is desired; none becomes an automatic persistent effect for later encounters merely from one play.

after_question.question: After being played once, do Anti-Matter Super, Cudgel Super, Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super, or Machine Wild automatically apply in later encounters, or must the corresponding flare be played again each encounter its effect is desired? For otherwise legal uses, what timing phrases does the official FAQ quote for the effects of Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super and Cudgel Super? For the first three, does the quoted wording refer to every player's Regroup or to the user's own Regroup phases?

required_facts: Each listed flare must be played in each encounter in which its effect is desired; none becomes an automatic persistent effect for later encounters merely from one play.
Kamikaze Super, Machine Super and Masochist Super quote during each of your Regroup phases: the user's own Regroup phases, not every player's.
Miser Super quotes at the start of each of your encounters.
Cudgel Super quotes whenever you use your power.
contextual_background: These are the quoted effect timing/owner/event clauses, not a reconstruction of when the flare may first be placed faceup or of its absent full effect, role, prerequisites, cost or target. Miser's start-of-each-own-encounter wording is not relabeled as the once-per-turn Start Turn step.

after_question.question: For the Fido flare effect specifically described in the official FAQ as forcing a player to draw from the discard pile, does the card come from the top of that pile, at random, or from a freely chosen position?

required_facts: The forced draw described by the FAQ takes the top card of the discard pile.
contextual_background: The source calls this Fido flare without identifying Wild versus Super. No full trigger, role, phase, target-selection permission, cost or remaining effect is supplied.
source_references: 2018 FAQ p4 extraction lines280–287, Fido flare described as forcing a top-discard draw.
